summary: 1934 L-4 cab on a stone base on Boise NF's Red Mountain; last staffed 1967 and later removed, with sources split on the year.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a stone base
facts.status_note: Removed; sources give no year or disagree (a 1968 emergency entry, a 1983 removal in a presentation). A climbers' page describes the old foundation on the summit.

access.note: Trailhead page shows 'Site Open' on Forest Service land, but lists operating hours as Memorial Day to Labor Day, which had ended by 2026-10-10. A closure notice for the Crooked Fire area is posted, and the page does not say whether it reaches the Red Mountain trail.

visit.trail_note: From the Clear Creek road out of Lowman, FS trail 145 for 2 miles to a junction, then trail 143 for 1.5 miles to the summit (SummitPost).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Rex's page says removed with no year; firelookout.com has an 'Emergency 1968' entry and calls it gone; the Boise NF presentation says removed 1983. The story gives all three without choosing one.
The only description of remains is the undated SummitPost page. The story attributes it to that page and says no other source describes the summit now.

notes_for_editor: Removal year is the main open question: 1968 (firelookout.com, unexplained 'Emergency' note), 1983 (Boise NF presentation, a secondary document on DocsLib that may be a partial copy), and no year on the Rex's page. The foundation remark comes from a user-written climbing page with no date. The Forest Service trailhead banner is dated 'Sept. 19' with no year. The page also lists operating hours of Memorial Day to Labor Day, which had ended by 2026-10-10, so the story gives those hours next to the 'Site Open' status and tells visitors to check with the Lowman Ranger District. The SummitPost route note mentions a Clear Creek road distance but the story does not repeat it. No photos added.
